findings.title: Skip of the busy-time check on days with a date override
Slots rejected on days with more than one override or working-hours range
"Unavailable all day" check compares Dayjs objects by reference
Slot end time ignored in the override and working-hours checks
Override day matched by UTC calendar date, not the organizer's local date
Override shifted to the invitee time zone can wrap past midnight

response:
## 1) Severity: CRITICAL | Type: Bug
Title: Skip of the busy-time check on days with a date override

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:133-135

Explanation:
When a slot falls on a day that has a date override and inside its range, the function returns `true` straight away. The `busy.every(...)` check never runs. Existing bookings and busy events from external calendars are ignored on those days, so the host can be double-booked.

The override check should only rule slots out. If the slot passes, the code should still fall through to the busy check.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
if (dateOverrideExist) {
  // within override: skip working-hours check, but still check busy times
  return busy.every(isNotOverlapping);
}
// or restructure: only skip the workingHours block when dateOverrideExist
if (!dateOverrideExist && workingHours.some(/* outside */)) return false;
return busy.every(...);
~~~

## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Slots rejected on days with more than one override or working-hours range

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:105-131
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:138-151

Explanation:
Both checks use `find`, which rejects the slot as soon as any single range on that day does not contain it. A day can have several ranges, for example 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00. A 14:00 slot lies outside the first range, so it is rejected even though the second range contains it.

The logic should be: reject only when the slot is outside every range for that day.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const overridesForDay = dateOverrides.filter(d => sameDay(d, slotStartTime));
if (overridesForDay.length) {
  const inside = overridesForDay.some(d =>
    !start(d).isSame(end(d)) &&
    !slotStartTime.isBefore(start(d)) && !slotEndTime.isAfter(end(d)));
  if (!inside) return false;
} else {
  const hoursForDay = workingHours.filter(w => w.days.includes(slotStartTime.day()));
  const inside = hoursForDay.some(w => startMin >= w.startTime && endMin <= w.endTime);
  if (!inside) return false;
}
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: "Unavailable all day" check compares Dayjs objects by reference

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114

Explanation:
`dayjs(a) === dayjs(b)` compares two newly created objects, so it is always `false`. A full-day-off override (start equals end) is therefore never detected here. Such overrides are only partly caught by the later checks. A slot starting exactly at the override start is neither before the start nor after the end, so it is still offered.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
if (dayjs(date.start).isSame(dayjs(date.end))) return true;
~~~

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Slot end time ignored in the override and working-hours checks

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:123
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:141-143

Explanation:
In the working-hours check, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime`, not `slotEndTime`. A slot that starts inside working hours but runs past the end is accepted.

The override check has the same problem. It tests `slotStartTime.isAfter(date.end)`, so a slot that starts inside the override but ends after it is accepted.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const end = slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute();
...
if (slotEndTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))) return true;
~~~

## 5) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Override day matched by UTC calendar date, not the organizer's local date

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:107-111
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:140

Explanation:
The override start is converted to real UTC, and only its UTC date (`YYYY MM DD`) is compared with the slot's UTC date. For organizers far from UTC, one local day spans two UTC dates. Slots on the other UTC date are not recognised as belonging to the override day. They fall through to the working-hours check and may be offered or blocked incorrectly.

The working-hours check has a related risk: it uses `slotStartTime.day()` and hours in UTC. That is only correct if the `workingHours` passed in are expressed in UTC. That depends on code outside this diff.

A better approach is to compare the slot against the override's full UTC interval rather than its date string.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const overrideDayStart = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).startOf("day");
const sameDay = slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone).isSame(overrideDayStart, "day");
~~~

## 6) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Override shifted to the invitee time zone can wrap past midnight

Affected:
- packages/lib/slots.ts:211-225

Explanation:
`startTime` and `endTime` are minutes-of-day taken after adding the invitee offset. When the shift crosses midnight (for example, organizer 20:00–23:00 shifted by +6h), `startTime` becomes greater than `endTime`, giving an invalid range. The override's slots are lost or produced on the wrong day.

There are two further problems:
- When `override.timeZone` is undefined (it is optional in `TimeRange`), `dayjs(...).tz(undefined)` falls back to the default or server time zone. That can produce a wrong offset.
- `dayjs(override.start.toString())` parses the non-ISO `Date.toString()` output, which is fragile. Use `dayjs(override.start)` instead.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const organizerTz = override.timeZone ?? "UTC";
const start = dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute");
const end = dayjs(override.end).utc().add(offset, "minute");
// handle cross-midnight: split into two ranges or keep absolute datetimes instead of minutes-of-day
~~~
